text.tspan: Two triggers, one shared reusable workflow.
Read top to bottom: it is a timeline.

g.text: ② LAUNCHED IMMEDIATELY AT t = 0 — 12 job definitions, not one `needs:` between them
③ THE ONLY JOBS THAT WAIT ON needs:

text.tspan: 15 min · JaCoCo shards + Vitest + Playwright → Codecov
best-effort, and deliberately NOT wired into the Gate
if: always() · needs: 14 jobs · Coverage excluded
→ POST rerun-failed-jobs on the same run
Loops back to ② as attempt 2 — exactly once
LEGEND — HOW TO READ THE ARROWS
▬▬▶ DARK SOLID = a real needs: in the YAML
waits for the entire upstream job to finish, artifact upload included
that is ~2.5 min of gzip / validate / upload the consumer never uses
only four edges in this whole pipeline are true needs:
╍╍▶ ORANGE DASHED = polling wait, no needs: at all
the job starts at t = 0 and boots its service containers in parallel
then it loops on the GitHub API / GHCR until the payload appears
and self-aborts the moment the upstream job reports failure or cancelled
this is the trick that keeps the critical path short
╍╍▶ PURPLE DASHED = auto-retry, fires once, on attempt 1 only
DOCKER BUILD HAS NO ARROW FROM PREPARE BUNDLED ASSETS
it re-runs the asset preparation inline with upload-artifact: false
saving ~1.4 min at the head of the critical path
CORE vs NIGHTLY — THE ONLY THREE DIFFERENCES
Core: 8 cells — 7 balanced shards + a 'remaining' catch-all, Elasticsearch
Nightly: the same 8 run twice, on Elasticsearch AND OpenSearch
Core: 10 cells, standard image only, chrome/amd64 + chromium/arm64
sharded arsenals / multitenant / remaining, plus 4 infra cells
Nightly: 25 cells, std + ubi9, five browsers, amd64 + arm64
plus the OpenSearch variants and 7 infra cells
Core: reports findings, never blocks the Gate
Nightly: fails the Gate on high/critical findings and scanner errors

g.text: needs: API Tests, E2E, API Types Check
